meta.stream: Value distribution in a $100 purchase: physical retail vs e-commerce vs agentic commerce
meta.method: Web search summaries (search engine result extracts) only. Direct fetching of primary documents (sec.gov, federalreserve.gov, support.google.com, pages.stern.nyu.edu, about.ads.microsoft.com) was blocked by the session network policy, and the shared web-search budget was exhausted before all topics were covered. Figures marked kind=filing were reported in search extracts that quote or table the filing; they should be spot-checked against the primary filing before publication. Derived ratios are labelled 'derived' in context.

paramDefinitions.grossMargin: Merchant gross margin on the $100 item (% of price) before channel costs. For model M it is the third-party seller's product margin before marketplace fees.
paramDefinitions.cac: Merchant-paid customer acquisition / marketing cost attributable to the order (% of price), excluding marketplace ads (placementFee).
paramDefinitions.takeRate: Marketplace commission / referral fee (% of price).
paramDefinitions.placementFee: Paid placement, sponsored listings, retail-media or affiliate/referral fee paid to the platform or agent (% of price).
paramDefinitions.payment: Payment acceptance cost (% of price), including fixed per-transaction fee on $100.
paramDefinitions.agentFee: Fee to AI platform / agent operator for orchestrating or completing the purchase (% of price), or retailer's own inference/orchestration cost for model D.
paramDefinitions.fulfillment: Pick/pack/ship cost (% of price). For model P this slot carries store occupancy cost instead, because the shopper does last-mile.
paramDefinitions.returnsFraud: Net cost of returns processing, return abuse and payment fraud not already netted in reported gross margin (% of price).
paramDefinitions.incrementalConversion: Conversion uplift vs. the own-site e-commerce baseline E (percent change; 0 = same as E). Not an absolute conversion rate.
paramDefinitions.repeatRate: Probability (%) the same customer buys again from this merchant within 12 months via the same channel.
paramDefinitions.retention: Share (0-100) of the customer relationship (identity, data, direct re-marketing ability) the merchant retains.

meta.simulatorNote: Defaults are % of the $100 price. Contribution = grossMargin minus (cac+takeRate+placementFee+payment+agentFee+fulfillment+returnsFraud); it excludes store labour, tech and corporate SG&A, so model P overstates profit relative to reported 3-5% retail operating margins. benchmarkIds point to entries in benchmarks[].

valueCaptureHistory.finding: Retail media is highly concentrated: Amazon ~79.7% and Walmart ~8% of US retail media in 2025 (combined 84.2% in 2024), and they are forecast to take ~89% of incremental 2026 spend.

Amazon's advertising revenue reached $68.6B in 2025 (+22%), alongside $172.2B in third-party seller services; together roughly 30-42% of estimated 3P GMV (~$575B). Ads now rival referral fees as a value-capture lever.

Marketplace take rates ratchet upward: Amazon's all-in share of seller revenue rose from ~1/3 (2016) to >50% (2022) per Marketplace Pulse; Etsy's take rate rose from 22.3% to 24.2% (2025) with ~25.5% guided for 2026.
Platform 'arms dealers' capture far less: Shopify revenue is ~3% of GMV (merchant solutions ~2.3%), versus 15-50% for marketplaces.
Retailer-owned agents extend incumbent retail media: Amazon's $10B Rufus incremental-sales estimate includes ads embedded in Rufus answers.

Third-party AI intermediaries have so far failed to impose a transaction toll: OpenAI's reported 4% checkout fee (Jan 2026) lasted ~2 months before Instant Checkout was deprioritized/ended in March 2026, while Microsoft (0% commission), Google UCP (no fee beyond processing per Shopify) and Perplexity (reported 0%) compete at zero. Monetization is drifting toward discovery/advertising, the Google search model, rather than a marketplace-style commission.

Payment networks are positioned to keep their toll in agentic commerce: agentic tokens ride standard interchange, Visa production fees are undisclosed, and US card acceptance fees reached a record ~$198B in 2025.

AI referrals are growing fast and convert better than other traffic (Adobe: from -9% in Mar 2025 to +42-60% in 2026), which is the demand-side precondition for AI platforms to charge for placement, but reliability benchmarks (29-75% task success) argue against fully delegated checkout capturing share quickly.

conflicts: OpenAI fee: launch announcement (2025-09-29) said 'small fee' without a rate; The Information/PYMNTS reported 4% for Shopify merchants from Jan 2026 (effective date reported as 2026-01-26 by some, 2026-02-16 by others); an Altman remark suggested ~2%. Status: Instant Checkout deprioritized 2026-03-05 (TechCrunch) / confirmed ended 2026-03-20 (CNBC); one commentary says removed 2026-03-04.

Current Shopify-ChatGPT fee: secondary sources cite Shopify Help Center 'no added fees beyond standard payment processing', but Shopify's supplemental terms reportedly allow a per-channel agentic fee at Shopify's discretion with promotional waivers.

Adobe holiday 2025 AI conversion: Adobe recap says +54% on Thanksgiving; secondary coverage says +31% for the season. 2026 monthly figures (+42% Mar, +54% May, +60% Jul) partly from secondary summaries.
Amazon 2025 third-party seller services: $172.2B (most 10-K based sources) vs $175.2B and $184.1B (other aggregators). 3P GMV estimate $575B (Marketplace Pulse) vs $520B (AMZ Prep).
Amazon fulfillment ($109.1B) and shipping ($102.7B) for 2025 come from secondary sources; not verified against the 10-K (sec.gov blocked).
Damodaran Jan 2026 grocery operating margin: 1.85% vs 2.29% across two reproductions; gross margins (33.18% general, 26.31% grocery) from secondary tables.
Walmart FY2026 gross margin: 24.2% of net sales vs 24.9% of total revenue vs management's ~24.0%.
Target FY2025 adjusted operating margin: 4.6% (10-K table) vs 4.8% (press release summary).
Returns fraud: NRF says 9% of returns fraudulent; Appriss says 14.2% fraud+abuse (2% fraud, 12% abuse). Total returns: NRF $849.9B (forecast) vs Appriss $706B (2025).
Card fees: Nilson $187.2B (2024) / $198.25B (2025) vs CMSPI $236.4B (2024); average rate 1.57% vs 1.59% (year unclear).
Walmart Marketplace referral range: 6-15% (Walmart page) vs 6-20% (third-party guides); reported June 2026 cuts in 14 categories unverified.
Amazon FBA 2026: Amazon says average +$0.08/unit; one third-party source says most standard-size rates decreased slightly.
Rufus: $10B incremental annualized sales (Q3 2025 call) vs ~$12B and rename to Alexa for Shopping (single 2026 source).
Perplexity Merchant Program 0% fees rests on a single secondary source.
Mercado Libre commerce revenue/GMV (~25%) overstates take rate because commerce revenue includes 1P sales and shipping.
Etsy 2025 marketing (~$915M) not verified against the 10-K.
